identity.title: ALMA 200 pc Resolution Imaging of Smooth Cold Dusty Disks in Typical z ∼ 3 Star-forming Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present high-fidelity, 30 milliarcsecond (200-pc) resolution ALMA rest-frame 240 $\mu$m observations of cold dust emission in three typical main-sequence star-forming galaxies (SFGs) at $z \sim 3$

question.value: Do typical main-sequence z~3 star-forming galaxies show star-forming dust clumps/substructures at 200-pc resolution, and how do they compare with SMGs?

evidence.quote: No dust substructures or clumps are seen down to $\simeq 1- 3$ $M_\odot$yr$^{-1}$ (1$\sigma$) per 200-pc beam.

findings_qualitative.value: Cold dust is smooth, well fit by two concentric Gaussians, with no emission at UV clump positions

claims.hypothesis: Typical z~3 SFGs host star-forming dust clumps at 200 pc scale
claims.experiment: 30 mas ALMA 870 um imaging and uv-plane modeling of three HUDF SFGs
claims.result: Residuals show no >=3 sigma peaks; clump upper limits 1-7% of SFR
claims.finding: Dust disks are smooth; no substructures

evidence.quote: Clumpy substructures can contribute no more than $1-7$% of the total star formation in these galaxies (3$\sigma$ upper limits).

claims.hypothesis: UV-bright clumps are sites of significant obscured star formation
claims.result: No dust emission at UV clumps 2-10 kpc away
claims.finding: UV clumps are not dust-obscured star-forming sites

evidence.quote: No dust emission is observed at the locations of UV-emitting clumps

claims.hypothesis: SMG substructures differ from those in typical SFGs
claims.experiment: Same uv analysis on H19 data
claims.result: SMGs need multiple extra components containing 10-30% SFR
claims.finding: SMGs may arise from more disruptive events involving multiple objects

evidence.quote: suggesting that these SMGs originate from a class of disruptive event involving multiple objects at the scale of our HUDF galaxies
